Afzal Khan vs State Of Up And 2 Others on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126302125/ 1 Court No. - 9 Hon'Ble Arun Kumar, J. 1.
texts.facts: 2. The present petition has been filed by the petitioner challenging the order of the respondent no. 2, dated 21.5.2024 and the order of the respondent no. 3, dated 25.10.2024, whereby the licence of the petitioner for running a retail outlet business of selling meat and meat products including poultry farm has been suspended. 3. Counsel for the petitioner contended that the petitioner was running the business on his own bhumidhari land having Plot No. 679, situated in Gram Pilibhit Mustkil, Tehsil and District Pilibhit. It is submitted that one Mohd. Shakeel Khan filed a complaint before the Prescribed Authority, Regulated Area, Pilibhit with the allegation that the petitioner is running his business of selling meat and meat products near abadi over Plot No. 686/2 and 686/2. 4. Pursuant to the aforesaid complaint notices were issued to the petitioner by the respondent no. 2 under the Uttar Pradesh (Regulation of Building Operations) Act, 1958 calling upon him to show cause that on the basis of the licence issued to him he is carrying on business on the land comprised over Gata No. 686. 5. It is submitted by the counsel for the petitioner that the said notice was never served upon the petitioner. The respondent no. 2 by his order dated 21.5.2025, under Section 32 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, suspended the licence of the petitioner for running the retail business of meat and meat products. 6. Aggrieved by the order of the respondent no. 2, dated 21.5.2024, the petitioner filed an appeal before the respondent no. 3, under Section 32(4)(c) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. 8. It is submitted that the appellate authority while dismissing the appeal of the petitioner has observed that a letter dated 8.10.2024 was issued to the Sub Divisional Magistrate, Sadar requesting him to conduct the demarcation of Plot No. 679 and 686 so that the claim of the petitioner could be decided, in accordance with law. However, without waiting for the report from the SDM Sadar the respondent no. 3 has dismissed the appeal of the petitioner holding that the petitioner has failed to Afzal Khan vs State Of Up And 2 Others on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126302125/ 2 establish that he was running his meat shop over Plot No. 679. 9. Having perused the materials placed on record, I find that the order passed by the respondent no. 2 suspending the licence of the petitioner for running meat shop was without any opportunity of hearing and behind his back as the impugned order itself shows that no reply has been filed by the petitioner. The respondent no
texts.arguments: 7. It is contended by the counsel for the petitioner that the order of the respondent no. 2, dated 21.5.2024, was an ex-parte order, passed behind the back of the petitioner without affording any opportunity to show that he was running his business on the bhumidhari land recorded in the name of his father. . 3 while considering the appeal of the petitioner has arrived at a conclusion that the actual dispute is with regard to identification of the plot no. 679 or 686 at which meat shop was running. Counsel for the petitioner has invited attention of the Court to Annexure 2 to the writ petition which is Khasra of Plot Nos. 686/1 and 686/2, showing that both the plots are in the form of drain.

Counsel for the petitioner has invited attention of the Court to Annexure 2 to the writ petition which is Khasra of Plot Nos. 686/1 and 686/2, showing that both the plots are in the form of drain.
